expectations.text: Rewrites the copy in the maintainer's first-person voice rather than a press-release register
expectations.evidence: The HN comment rewrite is squarely in maintainer first-person: "I'm [name], and I built Basalt after [the real problem you hit]...", "we sell a hosted version", "if it stops being useful without the paid product, that's a bug, tell us", "Happy to go deep on [specific technical area]". It explicitly diagnoses and strips the press-release register ("incredibly excited... game-changer... 10x faster" flagged as marketing copy, superlatives named and removed, unsourced numbers dropped, limitations disclosed, commercial relationship stated plainly). expectations.text: Rewrites the copy in the maintainer's first-person voice rather than a press-release register
expectations.evidence: Every rewrite drops the announcement register for a builder speaking directly. The HN rewrite opens "Hi HN, [name] here — one of the people building Basalt" and continues in plain first-person plural ("We built it after running into...", "We benchmarked it against Airflow... happy to hear where this doesn't hold up", "Happy to answer questions about the architecture"), including an unusually un-promotional self-hedge ("Self-reported vendor benchmarks deserve skepticism"). The one-liner rewrite likewise ends in maintainer voice — "self-host it free, or let us run it for you" — rather than third
